title: Not even a cold can keep me from talking about the Smash musical beca...
transcript: All right. I am still a little sick, but I physically cannot wait any longer to talk about the smash musical. So let's go. I was one of the lucky few to win tickets to what they called an open rehearsal. But it really was basically a full run through of the musical. They ran through the show from start to finish. There was an intermission. Everyone was off book. They did the full choreography and staging. The only thing it really didn't have was a full set. But there was enough set pieces that they use that you could imagine what the set was supposed to look like for any given scene. So, of course, the question on everybody's mind, how was the show itself? And I am happy to report that the show is in really great shape. The book by Bob Martin and Rick Ellis is incredibly funny and has a ton of in theater jokes. I have one criticism of the book. It would probably be similar to a criticism that I have of the TV show, which is that it is trying to be both a comedy and a melodrama. And I think that it does the comedy aspect a lot better than the melodrama. So as a result, I think that it can feel totally inconsistent. And as they continue to refine it, I hope they lean more towards the comedy side and less towards the melodrama. However, I think the best part about The show was the choreography. They actually got the choreographer from the TV show to faithfully recreate all of the iconic dances from the show for the stage musical. And as a fan of the TV show, being able to see those dances live on stage so faithfully recreated was a dream come true. Pretty much all of these songs from bombshell that you know and love made the cut. The only one I was disappointed didn't make the cut was Lexington of 52nd Street, but pretty much every other song from bombshell that I liked was in the show in some capacity. Now, not all of the songs were sung all the way through. Some of them were just little snippets of songs that they're either rehearsing or in, like, a montage of sorts. And while I think that may be disappointing to some people, personally, I felt like we got just enough of each number for me to be satisfied. Of course, we gotta talk about the ending, which, no spoilers here, but it has been very controversial, and chances are you've heard some things about it. For me personally, the ending did not work. I mentioned total issues earlier in this video, and I definitely think those total issues are on full display and at the finale of the show. So it was less that I had an issue with the actual plot points that happen and more that, like, totally it didn't really work and was A little all over the place for me. But if they could just clean up the ending a bit and do some trimming here and there, I really think that this could be a big hit. Is in great shape, and I think it will be enjoyed by both fans of the show and people who have never seen the TV show.
reasoning: Reviewer recommends the show and says it's in great shape, praises choreography and book humor, but has notable criticisms about tonal inconsistency and the controversial ending not working.
